the box of nougat sits open on a worn wooden dining table beside a child's hand-packed rice ball and a bowl of plain steamed rice, set against a deep terracotta-orange wall, one hard late-afternoon beam from a window on the left throwing crisp long shadows of the box and the thick round slices across the table

a single thick round nougat slice snapped in half to show whole peanuts inside, held big in the foreground over a tomato-red kitchen counter with the sealed box beside it, hard side light from the right casting a sharp shadow of the crack and every peanut

the sealed box stands large on a living-room coffee table in front of a deep-sea-blue sofa, a laptop paused on a drama beside it, hard lamp light from the upper left laying a sharp shadow of the box across the wood, a few nougat slices unwrapped beside it

a stack of nougat slices leans against the box on a mint-green tiled kitchen counter, a hard shaft of morning sun from the left window striking the cracked edge of one slice so each peanut and its shadow stands out in sharp relief

the box and an open pouch of individually sealed nougat sit on a school-lunch table of scratched wood, a small hand reaching in for a slice, hard overhead-left light against a terracotta wall, crisp shadows of the fingers and the slices on the tabletop

close macro of a bitten nougat slice, the chewy stretch and peanut crunch visible, held toward the camera in front of the box, mustard-yellow kitchen wall behind, hard window light from the right cutting a deep shadow under the bite
